recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. If PA advances later restructuring such as FHIR-53234, apply it in the repository that currently owns ChargeItemDefinition rather than restoring or editing retired core source.
issue_request: FHIR-34621 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request for R5 asking that ChargeItemDefinition.instance allow association with HealthcareService, with ActivityDefinition and PlanDefinition already handled by FHIR-22120.
initial_application: The core source change was applied by e29e42f21c31925a9d496a2841aecfaae99f878e, adding HealthcareService to source/chargeitemdefinition/structuredefinition-ChargeItemDefinition.xml. The related FHIR-22120 commit b8b51c33e1319e14185cb4eeb1b80540b2fde501 had already added DeviceDefinition, ActivityDefinition, and PlanDefinition.
additional_context: The current HL7/fhir build no longer owns ChargeItemDefinition: source/fhir.ini omits it from [resources], source/metadataresource/metadataresource-introduction.xml links ChargeItemDefinition to the HL7 admin-incubator IG, and 71567db3ee039ac6977be5f96a7e013896569a36 removed source/chargeitemdefinition from core. The current admin-incubator StructureDefinition JSON still includes HealthcareService, ActivityDefinition, and PlanDefinition as ChargeItemDefinition.instance targets. A later same-element issue, FHIR-53234, remains Triaged and was not treated as a final applied reversal.
reconciliation: No HL7/fhir source was changed. The required core reconciliation is an empty audit commit because the historical core application is present in git history and any current ChargeItemDefinition source maintenance belongs in the external admin-incubator artifact, not the current core build.
